Adjusted view using the SLOOS: Overall tone shifts modestly more negative. While the FOMC statement highlights ongoing recovery and accommodative financial conditions supported by asset purchases and liquidity tools, the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey around this period reported widespread tightening of lending standards and terms for C&I and CRE loans, tighter standards for consumer credit (credit cards and autos), and weaker business loan demand. Banks cited elevated uncertainty and reduced risk tolerance, and many expected further tightening and deterioration in credit quality. These SLOOS findings suggest bank intermediation could constrain the flow of credit to businesses and some households despite accommodative policy, amplifying downside risks from COVID-19. Balancing the supportive policy stance with tighter bank lending and softer loan demand yields a somewhat more negative assessment than before.
